A.objective: Using only authoritative data-room sources, determine which represented billed revenue is associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with counterparty and contract identifiers as they appear in the sources.

universe_scope.evidence_boundary: Authoritative files in this data room only; no external knowledge or hidden oracle.
included_records: Represented billed revenue (invoices as recorded in billing sources)
Contracts and their counterparties as represented in contract sources
Invoice fields: invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status
excluded_or_non_qualifying: Revenue on invoices that cannot be linked to any counterparty with an active contract bearing acquisition-relevant conditions
Contracts that are not active under purpose policy (e.g., an expired statement of work is not an active contract)

format_constraints: Identifiers and field values as they appear in sources (subject to downstream rendering contracts).

world_eligible: Invoice referent with billed_name, amount, currency, period, status grounded in billing sources
Contract referent with source filename/identifier and textual clause content grounded in contract sources
Counterparty naming as represented on invoices and in contracts
Temporal/status facts about contracts and invoices as stated in sources (e.g., expiry, SOW status)
purpose_policy_only: Active contract: a contract that counts as in-force for this analysis; an expired statement of work is explicitly not active

Acquisition-relevant condition: contractual term that (a) requires consent or notice on change of control, (b) permits termination upon change of control, or (c) requires consent or notice before assignment (including assignment restricted except to affiliates, or assignment prohibited to a competitor)
Qualifying invoice: represented billed revenue whose counterparty is associated—under purpose rules—with an active contract containing at least one acquisition-relevant condition
Association disposition asserted vs unresolved (see epistemic_requirements)

epistemic_requirements: Invoice-to-contract/counterparty linkage may be asserted only when billed name and contract counterparty can be confidently associated.
Missing or uncertain identity is not a negative contractual finding: do not omit qualifying invoices solely because identity is unclear; do not assert a join without confidence.
Clause classification as acquisition-relevant is a purpose-interpretive judgment over grounded contract text, not a source-native label.
Active-contract classification applies purpose thresholds to world-grounded contract status facts.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Invoice is in scope for reporting but billed_name cannot be confidently associated with the contract counterparty.
allowed_unresolved_states.forbidden_inference: Must not treat unresolved association as evidence that no acquisition-relevant exposure exists.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Include every invoice that qualifies under purpose policy (represented billed revenue tied—asserted or unresolved—to a counterparty whose active contract contains acquisition-relevant conditions).
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: For each included invoice, populate invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status, contract_id, and association.
completeness_expectations.ordering_completeness: Full qualifying set present; sorted by invoice_id.
explicit_non_goals: Does not require exhaustive enumeration of all invoices in billing—only those meeting the acquisition-exposure criterion.
Does not require resolving every identity ambiguity in the data room.

purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: Expired statement of work is not an active contract.
purpose_specific_policies.identity_join_policy: Confident association required for association=asserted; otherwise association=unresolved.
purpose_specific_policies.negative_finding_policy: Do not treat missing identity as a negative contractual finding.

rendering_and_derivation_hints.note: Downstream contracts may map identity judgments and strip identifier prefixes; those are presentation/derivation policies, not world truth.

B.objective: Using only authoritative data-room sources, identify represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, the company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, report whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records, or whether identification remains unresolved.

universe_scope.evidence_boundary: Authoritative files in this data room only.

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort links by left, then right.

world_eligible: Existence of CRM accounts, billed names, registry rows, and contract filenames as grounded referents
Registered legal names and company numbers as stated in registry sources
Account and counterparty names as stated in CRM, billing, and contract sources
purpose_policy_only: Commercial relevance: which names/records must participate in the reconciliation graph for diligence (drives link inclusion, not ontology of legal personhood)
Mechanical legal-form variant tolerance: exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical matches
Similarity guardrail: distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party
Required connectivity: links needed to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the governing contract, and candidate registry legal entities for that relationship

epistemic_requirements: SAME_ENTITY requires confident positive identification as the same legal counterparty—not mere orthographic similarity.
DISTINCT requires confident positive identification as different legal counterparties.
UNRESOLVED is permitted and expected where evidence is insufficient; absence of a SAME_ENTITY judgment is not a DISTINCT judgment.
Do not globally merge records because two names look similar.
Identity judgments are bounded semantic assertions (ground with evidence packets per kernel); they are not closed-world negation over all possible pairs.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Pairwise identification between left and right cannot be confidently resolved to SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT.
allowed_unresolved_states.forbidden_inference: Must not infer DISTINCT or SAME_ENTITY from silence or weak similarity.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Include every link required to connect, for each commercially relevant relationship, CRM account → billed name → governing contract → candidate registry legal entity(ies).
completeness_expectations.pair_coverage: Not an all-pairs Cartesian product; only links mandated by the connectivity requirement and commercial relevance.
completeness_expectations.ordering_completeness: Full required link set present; sorted by left then right.
completeness_expectations.cross_purpose_dependency: Purpose C reuses these identifier forms and may inherit unresolved identity; B does not need to resolve all ambiguity for downstream purposes.

purpose_specific_policies.merge_policy: No global merge on fuzzy name match.
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_variant_policy: Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be reconciled mechanically.
purpose_specific_policies.trade_name_policy: Similar trade names across distinct registry entities do not imply SAME_ENTITY.
purpose_specific_policies.link_inclusion_policy: Emit links needed for CRM–billing–contract–registry connectivity for commercially relevant relationships.
purpose_specific_policies.symmetry_policy: Links are ordered pairs (left, right) for output; semantic identity judgment is symmetric in meaning though tuples may be emitted in canonical orientation.

C.objective: Using only authoritative data-room sources, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under purpose thresholds, citing active contracts, open invoices, and qualifying obligation kinds.

universe_scope.evidence_boundary: Authoritative files in this data room only.
included_records: Active contracts (per purpose policy) with exclusivity, auto-renewal, or rolling-term provisions
Counterparties identified using Purpose B identifier forms
excluded_or_non_qualifying: Expired contracts (do not create current dependency)
One-off paid historical invoices without an active contract

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort dependencies by contract_id. obligation_kinds is a sorted list.

world_eligible: Invoice open/closed status and identifiers as in billing sources
Contract text and metadata for exclusivity, renewal, and term provisions
Contract active/expired status as represented in sources
Counterparty references on contracts and invoices
purpose_policy_only: Current commercial relationship: presence of an open invoice OR an active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
Active contract: in-force under purpose rules (expired contracts excluded)
Commercial dependency: BOTH (1) current commercial relationship AND (2) active contract contains exclusivity OR term auto-renewal OR rolling term continuing unless notice is given
Obligation kind taxonomy: exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term
Dependency status dependent vs unresolved (identity join uncertainty)

epistemic_requirements: Joining invoice and contract to the same counterparty may require identity judgments; if that identity is unresolved, report status=unresolved rather than status=dependent or implicit false.
Classifying exclusivity, auto-renewal, and rolling-term provisions is interpretive over grounded contract text.
Open invoice and active contract facts are world-grounded; the dependency composite is a purpose-defined predicate.
Historical one-off paid invoices without a continuing active contract do not satisfy the current-relationship leg of dependency.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Candidate dependency cannot be affirmed because identity needed to join invoice and contract (or counterparty attribution) is unresolved.
allowed_unresolved_states.forbidden_inference: Must not report unresolved as non-dependent or as dependent.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Report each contract-centric dependency row where either (a) both dependency legs are satisfied → status=dependent, or (b) dependency is blocked solely by unresolved identity → status=unresolved.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: For each row: counterparty, contract_id, open_invoice_ids (possibly empty), obligation_kinds (sorted subset of allowed kinds), status.
completeness_expectations.ordering_completeness: Full dependency set under policy; sorted by contract_id.
explicit_non_goals: Does not require resolving all Purpose B identity links.
Does not treat expired contracts or isolated historical invoices as current dependency.

purpose_specific_policies.current_relationship_rule: Open invoice OR active contract with auto-renewal or rolling term.
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
purpose_specific_policies.historical_invoice_rule: One-off paid historical invoice without active contract does not establish current relationship.
purpose_specific_policies.dependency_conjunction_rule: Commercial dependency requires both current relationship and qualifying obligation on the active contract.
purpose_specific_policies.identity_dependency_rule: Reuse Purpose B identifier forms; unresolved identity forces status=unresolved, not false.
